title: Retirement as a Local Resource
source_title: Across China: After retirement, many in China are finding new purpose
source_verification: 页面可访问；核验了退休居民参与志愿服务、纸质便民手册、上门提醒及社区互助等事实。
adaptation_note: 题材参考所列新华社英文网公开事实；本站原创改写，非媒体原文，非历年真题。
content:
Retirement is often described as the end of paid work. In one neighborhood, however, it has also become a new beginning for public service. Older residents visit neighbors, share useful information and organize activities. Their experience is treated as a resource rather than something left behind.

The volunteers do not assume that every service should move online. Some residents over 80 find smartphone searches difficult. A face-to-face reminder about a health check can reach them more easily. The community has also printed a handbook with bus routes, service locations and emergency contacts. This modest tool remains useful because readers can open it without a password, signal or unfamiliar screen.

Older volunteers receive support as well as giving it. Family doctors visit residents with limited mobility, while community workers check on people who live alone. Mutual-aid groups offer company to members facing illness. The arrangement is reciprocal: people may contribute in one situation and need assistance in another.

The larger lesson is not that retirement must stay busy. It is that communities should leave several doors open for participation. When older people can choose a suitable role, retirement may bring purpose without denying their own need for care.

questions.question: What reciprocal role can retired residents play locally?
options: All public information should be moved to smartphones
Older residents can contribute to community life while still receiving support
Retirement should require unpaid full-time work

questions.explanation: 全文说明退休居民既能贡献经验和服务，也可能接受医疗与社区支持。
questions.evidence_text: The arrangement is reciprocal: people may contribute in one situation and need assistance in another.

questions.question: Why did the community print a handbook?
options: To advertise private products
To provide practical information without requiring digital skills
To record the volunteers' work hours
To replace visits by family doctors
questions.explanation: 第二段说明纸质手册让不熟悉智能手机的老人也能查公交、服务点和紧急联系方式。
questions.evidence_text: The community has also printed a handbook with bus routes, service locations and emergency contacts.

questions.question: What does “reciprocal” most nearly mean here?
options: Limited to medical treatment
Controlled by a mobile application
Based on exchange in both directions
Performed for payment
questions.explanation: 冒号后解释了居民在不同情境下既可能贡献，也可能需要帮助，因此指双向互助。
questions.evidence_text: The arrangement is reciprocal: people may contribute in one situation and need assistance in another.

questions.question: What can be inferred about face-to-face reminders?
options: They are required for every resident
They make printed information unnecessary
They work only during health emergencies
They remain valuable when digital access is difficult
questions.explanation: 文中用高龄居民难以使用手机搜索来说明面对面提醒仍有不可替代的可及性。
questions.evidence_text: A face-to-face reminder about a health check can reach them more easily.

questions.question: Why should active retirement remain a choice rather than a duty?
options: As a reason to remove offline services
As proof that retired people no longer need care
As one possible source of purpose, not an obligation to remain busy
As less meaningful than paid employment
questions.explanation: 结尾明确限制了观点：不是要求退休必须忙碌，而是应提供可选择的参与角色。
questions.evidence_text: The larger lesson is not that retirement must stay busy.

title: Equal Service Is Not Identical Service
source_title: China Focus: China ramps up efforts to boost public welfare, address key social needs
source_verification: 页面可访问；核验了灵活就业者参保不受户籍限制、城市流入人口的服务需求以及公共服务向脆弱群体倾斜等事实。
adaptation_note: 题材参考所列新华社英文网公开事实；本站原创改写，非媒体原文，非历年真题。
content:
A city may promise the same public services to everyone, yet equal treatment does not always mean using one identical rule. A delivery rider, for example, may work for several platforms and change jobs often. If social insurance depends on a traditional long-term employer or a local household record, that worker can fall through the gap.

Recent welfare measures address such mismatches. They seek to let people in flexible employment join local insurance programs without residency restrictions. High-inflow cities are also expected to examine the practical needs of migrant workers, including schooling, housing and medical care. The purpose is not to create a separate system for every group. It is to remove rules that block people whose lives no longer fit an older pattern.

This approach also changes how fairness is measured. Counting the number of offices or websites tells little if the intended users cannot enter them. Officials must ask who remains absent and why. A service may need longer opening hours, simpler documents or support in another location.

Public welfare is therefore less like handing out identical coats and more like making sure everyone can reach shelter. The standard is a shared level of protection; the route toward it may reasonably differ.

questions.question: How can public services be equally protective without being identical?
options: They should be limited to workers with one employer
They may require different routes to reach a common level of protection
They are best measured by the number of government websites
They must use identical procedures in every city
questions.explanation: 全文论证公平并不等于程序完全相同，而是应消除不同群体面对的实际障碍，使其达到共同保障水平。
questions.evidence_text: The standard is a shared level of protection; the route toward it may reasonably differ.

options: They cannot change delivery platforms
They are forbidden to use city medical services
They may not fit insurance rules built around stable employment or residency
They must own a home before entering school
questions.explanation: 首段指出，依赖传统长期雇主或本地户籍的参保规则可能让灵活就业者掉出保障范围。
questions.evidence_text: If social insurance depends on a traditional long-term employer or a local household record, that worker can fall through the gap.

questions.question: What does “mismatches” most nearly refer to in the second paragraph?
options: Arguments among several delivery companies
Differences in the price of public housing
Errors in counting government offices
Conflicts between old service rules and present ways of living
questions.explanation: 前文描述新型灵活就业生活与旧有参保条件不吻合，因此该词指规则和现实之间的错位。
questions.evidence_text: Recent welfare measures address such mismatches.

questions.question: Why does the author question counting offices or websites?
options: Every public office should stay open all night
Most residents refuse to visit public offices
Websites always cost more than face-to-face services
Their number does not show whether intended users can actually obtain the service
questions.explanation: 由“数量说明不了用户能否进入”可推断，投入或渠道数量不能替代可及性的结果判断。
questions.evidence_text: Counting the number of offices or websites tells little if the intended users cannot enter them.

questions.question: Why can simpler documents support equal public protection?
options: As unfair rewards for one profession
As reasonable tools for removing access barriers
As evidence that common standards should disappear
As temporary substitutes for all public institutions
questions.explanation: 作者把简化材料、延长时间等视为帮助不同群体达到共同保障水平的合理路径。
questions.evidence_text: A service may need longer opening hours, simpler documents or support in another location.

title: A Smart Device Still Needs a Human Plan
source_title: China Focus: How technology powers China's drive for common prosperity
source_verification: 页面可访问；核验了养老机构使用智能药盒和行为、生命体征数据识别风险，以及浙江数字平台连接超过4万家养老服务机构等事实。
adaptation_note: 题材参考所列新华社英文网公开事实；本站原创改写，非媒体原文，非历年真题。
content:
A smart pill box can remind an older resident to take medicine. A sensor can notice an unusual change in movement or vital signs. These tools may help caregivers see a risk earlier, but the device does not decide what good care means.

That decision belongs to people. A nursing home must choose who receives an alert, how quickly staff respond and when a family or doctor should be contacted. If a system produces too many warnings, workers may stop trusting it. If it collects data without clear limits, residents may lose privacy while gaining little protection.

Scale creates another challenge. One digital platform in Zhejiang links tens of thousands of senior-service providers. A wide network can spread useful methods and connect residents with nearby help. However, adding more institutions to a screen is not the same as improving every visit. Staff training, reliable equipment and an offline way to ask for help still matter.

Technology is most valuable when it supports a clear care process. The question should not be whether a home looks modern. It should be whether residents are safer, better understood and still treated as people who can make choices about their own lives.

questions.question: What is the central message of the passage?
options: Sensors should replace staff in nursing homes
A large platform automatically improves every care visit
Care technology works best inside a responsible human process
Older residents should avoid all digital equipment
questions.explanation: 文章反复强调设备只能辅助，回应、隐私、培训和居民选择仍需由清晰的人本流程保障。
questions.evidence_text: Technology is most valuable when it supports a clear care process.

questions.question: What problem may follow from too many system warnings?
options: Families will receive free equipment
Residents will take more medicine
The platform will add more institutions
Workers may begin to distrust the alerts
questions.explanation: 第二段直接说明警报过多可能导致工作人员不再信任系统。
questions.evidence_text: If a system produces too many warnings, workers may stop trusting it.

questions.question: What does “Scale” refer to at the start of paragraph three?
options: A device for measuring body weight
The size and reach of the service network
The speed of a medical response
A score given to nursing homes
questions.explanation: 紧接着介绍连接数万家服务机构的平台，因此指网络覆盖规模。
questions.evidence_text: Scale creates another challenge.

questions.question: What can be inferred about an offline way to seek help?
options: It is needed only when equipment is new
It protects access when a resident cannot use the digital channel
It prevents staff from receiving training
It makes the digital platform unnecessary
questions.explanation: 作者把线下求助与培训、可靠设备并列为必要条件，说明数字渠道不能覆盖所有人的使用情境。
questions.evidence_text: Staff training, reliable equipment and an offline way to ask for help still matter.

questions.question: Which test of technology does the author favor?
options: Whether it makes a building appear modern
Whether it gathers as much data as possible
Whether it improves safety, understanding and resident choice
Whether every warning reaches a family member
questions.explanation: 结尾明确把安全、理解和自主选择作为评价标准，而不是现代化外观。
questions.evidence_text: It should be whether residents are safer, better understood and still treated as people who can make choices about their own lives.

title: A Ramp Is an Invitation to Participate
source_title: Nation clears barriers for its disabled
source_verification: 页面可访问；核验了无障碍家庭改造、残疾人职业培训和就业，以及无障碍环境建设法支持社会参与等事实。
adaptation_note: 题材参考所列 China Daily 公开事实；本站原创改写，非媒体原文，非历年真题。
content:
A step at the entrance of a shop may look small to most customers. To a wheelchair user, it can decide whether the entire building is available. Accessibility therefore concerns more than construction. It determines who can study, work, shop and join public life without asking to be carried.

Home renovation offers a clear example. A handrail, a wider doorway or a safer bathroom can reduce daily risk. Yet improvements outside the home are equally important. Training gives a person useful skills, but an inaccessible bus or workplace may still keep that person from a job. Welfare payments provide support, but they cannot replace the freedom to enter a school or service center independently.

This is why barrier-free rules matter. They turn access from a kind favor into a normal expectation. A useful inspection should also involve the people who meet the obstacles. A ramp may follow a drawing and still be too steep; a sign may exist and still be impossible to read.

Good access often becomes ordinary and almost invisible. That is a success, not a reason to ignore it. When a building welcomes different bodies without special negotiation, participation begins at the front door.

questions.question: How does a ramp change participation beyond physical entry?
options: It is mainly a style of modern building design
It removes the need for vocational training
It concerns only private homes
It enables independent participation in everyday social life
questions.explanation: 全文把无障碍与学习、工作、出行和公共参与联系起来，强调独立参与而非单纯建筑形式。
questions.evidence_text: Accessibility therefore concerns more than construction.

questions.question: Why might job training fail to lead to employment?
options: Welfare rules forbid trained people to work
The trainee may dislike the new skill
Transport or the workplace may remain inaccessible
Every employer requires a wider home doorway
questions.explanation: 第二段指出，即使掌握技能，无障碍公交或工作场所的缺失仍可能阻止就业。
questions.evidence_text: Training gives a person useful skills, but an inaccessible bus or workplace may still keep that person from a job.

questions.question: In the front-door example, what burden does negotiation describe?
options: Discussing the price of a new building
Having to request and arrange special help
Applying for a training course
Testing the strength of a handrail
questions.explanation: 语境是建筑本应直接欢迎不同身体条件的人，无需临时请求并协调特殊帮助。
questions.evidence_text: When a building welcomes different bodies without special negotiation, participation begins at the front door.

questions.question: Why should users take part in accessibility inspections?
options: Only wheelchair users understand construction costs
Inspectors are not allowed to read building plans
A design can meet a drawing yet remain difficult to use
Users can replace every safety rule with personal preference
questions.explanation: 坡道可能图纸合规却过陡，说明真实使用者能发现形式检查遗漏的可用性问题。
questions.evidence_text: A ramp may follow a drawing and still be too steep; a sign may exist and still be impossible to read.

questions.question: How do barrier-free rules change access from kindness into expectation?
options: They are useful only during home renovation
They make welfare support unnecessary
They draw too much attention to ordinary buildings
They establish access as an expected right rather than a favor
questions.explanation: 作者肯定规则把无障碍从善意帮助转变为正常社会预期。
questions.evidence_text: They turn access from a kind favor into a normal expectation.

title: The Toolroom That Became a Shared Table
source_title: Across China: Community partners drive innovative grassroots governance
source_verification: 页面可访问；核验了废弃工具房改成邻里服务中心、引入商户和居民提供早餐及日用品，以及政府、市场、社会协同治理等事实。
adaptation_note: 题材参考所列新华社英文网公开事实；本站原创改写，非媒体原文，非历年真题。
content:
An abandoned toolroom in a crowded neighborhood once served nobody. After a local partnership reopened it, the small space began selling breakfast, vegetables and daily necessities. Older residents could rest outside after exercise, while commuters collected food on their way to work.

The change did not come from one office planning every detail. Community officials provided a place and invited merchants, residents and social groups to propose services. A local business could earn income while meeting a public need. Residents could also join cleaning, maintenance or cultural activities. The result was neither a fully commercial shop nor a traditional government counter.

Such partnerships can use forgotten spaces and local knowledge, but they need rules. A popular service should not push out residents who cannot pay much. Partners must explain prices, responsibilities and how complaints will be handled. Officials still have to protect basic access rather than assuming that any busy business equals good community service.

The toolroom matters because it changed relationships as well as walls. People who once appeared only as service users became workers, organizers and decision-makers. A shared neighborhood grows stronger when residents help shape what happens close to home.

options: Older residents prefer shopping to outdoor exercise
Every community service should become a private shop
Government offices should stop protecting basic access
Local partnerships can turn unused space into shared services and participation
questions.explanation: 文章通过工具房改造说明多方合作既能盘活空间和服务，也能让居民参与社区建设。
questions.evidence_text: The toolroom matters because it changed relationships as well as walls.

questions.question: What role did community officials play?
options: They set every breakfast price
They offered a place and invited different groups to suggest services
They required residents to work in maintenance
They closed all traditional government counters
questions.explanation: 第二段明确写到社区人员提供场地，并邀请商户、居民和社会团体提出服务方案。
questions.evidence_text: Community officials provided a place and invited merchants, residents and social groups to propose services.

questions.question: What does “push out” mean in paragraph three?
options: Employ for cleaning
Invite to complain
Exclude or displace
Move outdoors for exercise
questions.explanation: 语境担心热门服务排斥支付能力较弱者，因此指排除或挤走。
questions.evidence_text: A popular service should not push out residents who cannot pay much.

questions.question: Why does the author say a busy business may not equal good service?
options: Busy shops never meet a public need
Residents dislike services that earn income

Commercial success does not guarantee fair basic access

questions.evidence_text: Officials still have to protect basic access rather than assuming that any busy business equals good community service.

questions.question: Under what condition do community partners improve the shared toolroom?
options: Positive, provided that access and accountability are protected
Negative because merchants always control decisions
Uncertain because unused spaces have no social value
Positive only when residents remain passive users
questions.explanation: 作者肯定合作盘活资源和居民参与，同时明确需要价格、责任、投诉和基本可及性规则。
questions.evidence_text: Such partnerships can use forgotten spaces and local knowledge, but they need rules.

title: A Care Center That Extends into the Street
source_title: China Focus: Friendly community built for seniors with cognitive impairments
source_verification: 页面可访问；核验了中心活动、服务人数、周边商户参与、早期筛查与连续照护网络等事实。
adaptation_note: 题材参考所列新华社英文网公开事实；本站重新确定中心问题并原创改写，非媒体原文，非历年真题。
content:
A service center for older people with cognitive impairments might be imagined as a quiet medical room. A center in Shanghai follows a different model. It includes a cafe, art, virtual reality, music and other activities. During its first year, it organized more than 300 events and served over 2,000 people.

The design recognizes that care is not limited to diagnosis. Regular stimulation and social contact can help some older adults maintain everyday abilities. Families may also benefit when a relative can take part in a safe activity outside the home. Yet the most important feature may be the center's relationship with the surrounding neighborhood. Nearby cafes, shops and banks participate in making their services easier for affected seniors to use.

This network changes the meaning of a “friendly” place. If support exists only inside one building, a visitor may lose it as soon as the door closes. When ordinary businesses learn how to respond, more of the street becomes navigable. Navigable here means possible to move through and use with less confusion.

Medical care still matters. Early screening can identify risks, and qualified institutions are needed for treatment. But a clinic cannot organize every hour of daily life. A useful system therefore links hospitals, community organizations, families and familiar public places. The center is valuable not because it hides vulnerable people from the city, but because it helps the city receive them.

questions.question: What made the Shanghai center different from a simple medical room?
options: It admitted only hospital patients
It offered social and creative activities
It closed all nearby businesses
It provided care only through virtual reality
questions.explanation: 首段列举咖啡、艺术、音乐等活动，说明中心并非只有诊疗功能。
questions.evidence_text: It includes a cafe, art, virtual reality, music and other activities.

questions.question: Which statement best captures the author's argument?
options: Medical diagnosis should be removed from cognitive care
Every shop should become a hospital department
Cognitive care works better as a connected neighborhood system
Older adults should remain inside one protected building
questions.explanation: 全文从中心延伸到商户、医院、家庭和社区，强调连接式照护。
questions.evidence_text: A useful system therefore links hospitals, community organizations, families and familiar public places.

questions.question: What does “navigable” mean in paragraph 3?
options: Designed for online shopping
Reserved for trained nurses
Hidden from family members
Easy enough to move through and use
questions.explanation: 正文紧接着给出语境定义，即更少困惑地移动和使用。
questions.evidence_text: Navigable here means possible to move through and use with less confusion.

questions.question: Why are nearby shops and banks important to the model?
options: They extend support into ordinary daily activities
They can perform medical screening without training
They prevent seniors from returning home
They make family involvement unnecessary
questions.explanation: 作者指出若支持只在楼内，出门即消失；商户参与让街区日常活动更可达。
questions.evidence_text: When ordinary businesses learn how to respond, more of the street becomes navigable.

questions.question: What limited but continuing role does medical care have in the street-based system?
options: Unhelpful once art activities are available
Necessary but unable to cover every part of daily life
Suitable only for people without families
Less important than commercial services
questions.explanation: 末段肯定筛查和治疗，同时指出诊所不能安排全部日常生活。
questions.evidence_text: Medical care still matters.

title: A Longer Life Should Widen Choice
source_title: China steps up support for social participation of seniors amid population aging
source_verification: 页面可访问；核验了银龄志愿服务、老年大学与终身学习、为有意愿老年人提供多样就业与技能提升机会等事实。
adaptation_note: 题材参考所列新华社英文网公开事实；本站原创改写，非媒体原文，非历年真题。
content:
Policies on active aging often describe older people as a valuable social resource. The phrase can challenge the idea that retirement equals decline. Retired doctors may volunteer, former technicians may train younger workers, and senior students may discover subjects they had no time to study before.

Yet a positive message can become pressure if contribution is treated as a duty. Some people want paid part-time work; others prefer music classes, travel, family care or rest. Poor health may limit participation for a period. None of these choices makes a person less worthy of respect. A useful policy should expand possible roles without turning one picture of an energetic retirement into a new social rule.

Practical support makes that distinction real. Volunteer programs need insurance and suitable tasks, not only public praise. Training centers should admit older learners instead of assuming new skills belong to the young. Employers offering flexible positions must avoid using the language of purpose to justify low pay or unsafe conditions.

The strongest view of active aging is therefore based on agency. Longer lives give society more experience, but that experience belongs first to the people who gained it. Institutions can open doors and remove age barriers. Older adults should decide which door, if any, they wish to enter.

questions.question: What principle does the passage propose for active-aging policy?
options: It should direct every retiree into paid part-time work
It should value volunteering but discourage senior education
It should broaden older adults' choices without making participation compulsory
It should reserve skills training for younger workers
questions.explanation: 文章肯定拓展参与机会，但核心强调自主选择，不能把积极老龄化变成新的义务。
questions.evidence_text: A useful policy should expand possible roles without turning one picture of an energetic retirement into a new social rule.

questions.question: What protection does the author say volunteer programs need?
options: Guaranteed full-time jobs
Free international travel
The power to set retirement ages
Insurance and tasks suited to participants
questions.explanation: 第三段明确提出志愿项目需要保险和合适任务，而不只是口头表扬。
questions.evidence_text: Volunteer programs need insurance and suitable tasks, not only public praise.

questions.question: What does “agency” mean in the final paragraph?
options: The ability to make one's own choices
An office that hires volunteers
A measure of physical strength
A payment for professional experience
questions.explanation: 后文说明机构负责开门，老年人决定是否进入，故agency指自主决定能力。
questions.evidence_text: The strongest view of active aging is therefore based on agency.

questions.question: Why can purposeful jobs never excuse low pay or unsafe conditions?
options: All flexible positions are dangerous
Meaningful language can hide unfair treatment of older workers
Older adults care only about salary
Employers should replace work with music classes
questions.explanation: 作者警告雇主不能借“人生意义”之名为低薪或不安全开脱，可推断积极话语也需要劳动保障审视。
questions.evidence_text: Employers offering flexible positions must avoid using the language of purpose to justify low pay or unsafe conditions.

questions.question: Why does choosing rest leave a retired person equally worthy of respect?
options: As a sign of social decline
As acceptable only during training
As a legitimate choice
As less worthy than family care
questions.explanation: 作者把休息与学习、旅行等并列，并明确不同选择都不降低人的尊严。
questions.evidence_text: None of these choices makes a person less worthy of respect.

title: The Best Upgrade May Be a Familiar Home
source_title: China Focus: Chinese elderly embrace "silver" lives via age-friendly communities
source_verification: 页面可访问；核验了智能门锁、床头呼叫器和感应灯等居家改造，以及社区餐饮、日间照料与“15分钟”居家养老服务圈等事实。
adaptation_note: 题材参考所列新华社英文网公开事实；本站原创改写，非媒体原文，非历年真题。
content:
For an older person, moving into a care institution may provide safety but also remove familiar routines. Age-friendly communities try another path: adapt the home and bring support closer. A motion-sensor bathroom light can reduce a night-time fall. An emergency button can call family or community staff. A nearby dining hall makes a hot meal possible without a long journey.

These changes look modest beside a new hospital, yet they address the repeated moments that shape daily independence. Their value also depends on fit. A smart lock that helps one resident may confuse another. A handrail installed at the wrong height can satisfy a purchase list while failing the person who must use it. Home visits and conversation are therefore part of the design process, not an extra courtesy after equipment arrives.

Community services fill gaps that hardware cannot. Day-care rooms offer company and activities, while meal delivery supports residents with limited mobility. Health management can notice a changing need before an emergency. The aim is not to keep every older adult at home at any cost. Some will require specialized or continuous care.

A successful age-friendly neighborhood gives residents a real range of options. It connects housing, meals, health support and social life closely enough that staying home remains a safe choice rather than the result of having nowhere else to go.

questions.question: What model of eldercare does the passage describe?
options: Replacing all care institutions with smart locks
Moving every older resident near a hospital
Using purchase lists as the main measure of care
Adapting homes and nearby services to preserve safe choices

title: Designing by Memory, Touch and Sound
source_title: Across China: Retirement home lights up late life of the visually impaired
source_verification: 页面可访问；核验了视障老人养老机构的固定座位、桌面点字姓名牌、带点字的扶手，以及尊重个人饮食与兴趣等事实。
adaptation_note: 题材参考所列新华社英文网公开事实；本站原创改写，非媒体原文，非历年真题。
content:
A retirement home for people with visual impairments cannot rely on bright signs and attractive colors. Its residents navigate through memory, touch, sound and repeated routines. That changes what counts as thoughtful design.

In one specialist home, dining tables carry names in Braille at each corner. Fixed seats help residents know who is nearby, making conversation and movement more predictable. Raised markings on guardrails allow people to recognize locations while walking. Staff also record dietary preferences rather than treating blindness as the only fact that matters about a resident.

These details show why universal safety rules are only a starting point. A standard handrail can prevent a fall, but a tactile marker can also provide information. A clear corridor may satisfy an inspector, while an unexpected chair can still interrupt a route learned by memory. Good care requires workers to notice how residents actually use a space and to keep important arrangements consistent.

Consistency, however, should not become control. Residents still need opportunities to choose hobbies, companions and daily schedules. Predictable surroundings can support that freedom because less energy is spent discovering avoidable changes.

Inclusive design often begins with a different question. Instead of asking how a resident can adapt to an ordinary building, designers ask what the building must communicate through the senses that resident uses. The result can offer both safety and a stronger sense of belonging.

questions.question: What lesson about inclusive design does the passage draw from the specialist home?
options: Spaces should communicate through the senses their residents use
Visual signs should be made larger in every room
Fixed routines should remove all personal choice
Safety inspections can replace observation of residents

questions.evidence_text: designers ask what the building must communicate through the senses that resident uses.

options: They make meals shorter
They help residents know who is around them
They allow staff to change diets
They keep visitors outside the room

questions.evidence_text: Fixed seats help residents know who is nearby, making conversation and movement more predictable.

Changed without warning
Designed to be understood by touch
Checked by an inspector
questions.explanation: 该词修饰扶手上的标记，并与提供信息相连，语境指可通过触摸识别。
questions.evidence_text: A standard handrail can prevent a fall, but a tactile marker can also provide information.

options: It makes the corridor fail every building law
It prevents Braille from being read at dinner
It causes staff to change residents' hobbies
It can block a route a resident has memorized
questions.explanation: 文中强调视障住户借助记忆路线行动，因此突然变化的家具会破坏已掌握的空间线索。
questions.evidence_text: A clear corridor may satisfy an inspector, while an unexpected chair can still interrupt a route learned by memory.

questions.evidence_text: Consistency, however, should not become control.

title: Repairing a City Without Erasing It
source_title: China unveils guidelines on advancing urban renewal campaign
source_verification: 页面可访问；核验了旧住宅与厂区改造、停车充电消防和地下管网升级，以及城市历史文化保护和全生命周期房屋安全管理等事实。
adaptation_note: 题材参考所列新华社英文网公开事实；本站原创改写，非媒体原文，非历年真题。
content:
Urban renewal is sometimes pictured as a dramatic skyline filled with new towers. Much of the important work, however, happens underground or inside old neighborhoods. Water pipes leak, charging points are missing, fire routes are blocked and aging buildings need careful reinforcement. Solving these problems can improve daily life without replacing an entire district.

The difficulty is that a city is not an empty construction site. An old factory may hold jobs, memories or a distinctive street pattern. A commercial block may need safer wiring while its small shops need affordable rent. If renewal measures success only by new floor space, they can remove the relationships that made the area useful.

A better process begins with diagnosis. Engineers assess structural and pipeline risks. Residents identify inconvenient routes and missing services. Historians and local groups can explain which features carry shared meaning. These perspectives may disagree, so planners must publish priorities and show why one problem is addressed before another.

Repair also requires maintenance after the opening ceremony. A renovated drain can fail if nobody monitors it, and a public room can become empty if its operating budget disappears. Whole-life-cycle management treats buildings and services as continuing responsibilities rather than finished products.

Renewal succeeds when a neighborhood becomes safer and more useful while remaining recognizable to the people who live there. The goal is not to freeze a city in the past, but to let it change without forgetting what already works.

questions.question: What must urban renewal preserve while improving neighborhood safety?
options: Replacing old districts with taller buildings
Improving safety and usefulness while preserving valuable local relationships
Protecting every old feature from any change
Focusing investment only on underground pipes
questions.explanation: 全文主张通过诊断、参与和持续维护改善社区，同时保留已有价值而非大拆大建。
questions.evidence_text: Renewal succeeds when a neighborhood becomes safer and more useful while remaining recognizable to the people who live there.

questions.question: Who can explain which local features carry shared meaning?
options: Only building engineers
Charging-point manufacturers
Historians and local groups
Visitors at an opening ceremony
questions.explanation: 第三段明确把识别共同意义的角色交给历史研究者和本地群体。
questions.evidence_text: Historians and local groups can explain which features carry shared meaning.

questions.question: What does “diagnosis” mean in this planning context?
options: A medical check for construction workers
A vote to keep every old shop
A ceremony marking project completion
A careful identification of problems and needs
questions.explanation: 后文列举工程风险评估、居民指出不便和历史价值识别，说明指系统发现问题与需求。
questions.evidence_text: A better process begins with diagnosis.

questions.question: What risk follows if success is measured only by new floor space?
options: Useful community ties may be destroyed
Underground pipes will never be replaced
Engineers will refuse to assess buildings
Small shops will automatically receive lower rent
questions.explanation: 第二段指出这种单一指标可能清除使地区有用的关系，可推断物理增量会掩盖社会损失。
questions.evidence_text: If renewal measures success only by new floor space, they can remove the relationships that made the area useful.

questions.question: What does the author think of post-renovation maintenance?
options: It is less important than an opening ceremony
It is an essential continuing responsibility
It should be left entirely to residents
It matters only for public rooms
questions.explanation: 作者用排水和公共空间例子强调改造后仍需监测与运营资金，不能视为完工即结束。
questions.evidence_text: Whole-life-cycle management treats buildings and services as continuing responsibilities rather than finished products.

title: An AI Lesson About More Than Software
source_title: Across China: Retirees embrace AI via night schools
source_verification: 清单原URL失效；已核验新华社同题有效页面，确认22人课堂、老照片修复、社区课程与志愿教师网络等事实；正式清单需改用本条有效URL。
adaptation_note: 题材参考所列新华社英文网公开事实；本站依据有限事实原创改写，非媒体原文，非历年真题。
content:
In a night class in Shenzhen, 22 older students used an artificial-intelligence tool to repair faded photographs and make still images appear to move. The task looked playful, but it addressed a serious question: what kind of teaching allows people to enter a technological world that was not designed around their previous experience?

The answer was not a faster lecture. Students followed concrete instructions, compared results with neighbors and asked for help when a command failed. One learner had once struggled simply to find the place where a prompt should be typed. Step by step, she later moved among classes on text, images and video. Her progress illustrates a form of digital confidence built through repeated, meaningful tasks rather than abstract descriptions of AI.

The subject matter also mattered. Restoring an old photograph connected unfamiliar software with personal memory. That connection gave learners a reason to persist through confusion. It also turned the classroom into a social space: students showed one another their results instead of privately trying to keep pace with a machine.

Such courses have spread through community programs, some supported by volunteer instructors. Their value should not be measured only by the number of functions taught. A learner may forget a menu but remember how to ask a question, test an output and seek assistance. These are transferable habits, meaning they can be used in another digital task.

An age-friendly technology policy therefore needs more than larger text and simpler buttons. It needs places where older adults can learn without embarrassment, connect new tools with purposes they value and return for another attempt.

options: They should concentrate on memorizing every software menu

They build confidence when learning is practical, social and personally meaningful
They are valuable mainly because moving images are entertaining
questions.explanation: 文章从具体任务、同伴互动和个人记忆三个维度说明课程如何建立数字信心。
questions.evidence_text: Her progress illustrates a form of digital confidence built through repeated, meaningful tasks rather than abstract descriptions of AI.

questions.question: What did the 22 students do during the reported class?
options: They designed a new community center
They trained robots to teach video lessons
They compared different smartphone prices
They repaired old photographs with an AI tool
questions.explanation: 首句直接说明课堂使用AI修复褪色照片并让静态图像动起来。
questions.evidence_text: In a night class in Shenzhen, 22 older students used an artificial-intelligence tool to repair faded photographs and make still images appear to move.

questions.question: Why was photograph restoration a useful learning task?
options: It linked unfamiliar software to memories the learners cared about
It removed the need to understand any instructions
It guaranteed that every AI output was accurate
It allowed students to avoid working with classmates
questions.explanation: 由“个人记忆”带来坚持理由可推断，该任务用熟悉且有意义的目标降低了陌生技术的距离。
questions.evidence_text: That connection gave learners a reason to persist through confusion.

options: Skills owned by the software company

questions.evidence_text: These are transferable habits, meaning they can be used in another digital task.

options: Unnecessary because older adults learn alone
More important than any human instruction
Helpful but incomplete without supportive learning spaces
Harmful when combined with community classes

questions.evidence_text: An age-friendly technology policy therefore needs more than larger text and simpler buttons.

title: What an Elevator Number Cannot Tell Us
source_title: China spends big on urban renewal in 2025
source_verification: 页面可访问；核验了2025年旧小区改造及受益家庭、老楼加装电梯、口袋公园与城市绿道、地下管线建设改造等公开数据。
adaptation_note: 题材参考所列新华社英文网公开事实；本站原创改写，非媒体原文，非历年真题。
content:
Urban-renewal reports often feature impressive totals: residential compounds repaired, elevators installed, pocket parks opened and kilometers of pipeline replaced. Such figures are necessary. They show whether promised work happened and allow the public to compare spending with physical output. But a completed object is not identical to an improved life.

Consider an elevator added to an old apartment block. The project count rises by one, yet residents benefit only if the entrance is step-free, the controls are reachable and maintenance is affordable. A pocket park adds green space, but its social value depends on safe crossings, shade, seating and opening hours. Even underground pipes, invisible after construction, need monitoring if fewer leaks and service interruptions are the intended result.

Evaluation should therefore connect three layers. The first records delivery: what was built and at what cost. The second observes use: who enters, how often and what barriers remain. The third examines outcomes over time, such as safer movement, reliable water or reduced heat stress. These layers can reveal an uncomfortable result. A project may meet its engineering target while serving fewer residents than expected.

This does not make numerical targets useless. Without them, vague promises are difficult to challenge. The problem begins when the easiest quantity becomes the only definition of success. Good reporting should combine counts with residents' experiences and explain why benefits differ across streets or groups.

Urban renewal is public work carried out in lived places. Its final unit is not an elevator, park or pipe. It is a practical change that people can reach, use and continue to rely on.

questions.question: What improvement in urban-renewal evaluation does the author advocate?
options: Replacing all numerical targets with personal stories
Counting only projects that remain visible above ground
Measuring success entirely through engineering completion
Linking construction totals to use and long-term outcomes
questions.explanation: 文章主张交付、使用和长期结果三层结合，不能把物理数量直接等同于生活改善。
questions.evidence_text: Evaluation should therefore connect three layers.

questions.question: Which factor can affect the social value of a pocket park?
options: Safe crossings, shade, seating and opening hours
The number of underground pipes nearby
Whether an elevator was installed first
The price of water in another district
questions.explanation: 第二段直接列出过街安全、遮阴、座椅和开放时间会影响公园的真实社会价值。
questions.evidence_text: A pocket park adds green space, but its social value depends on safe crossings, shade, seating and opening hours.

questions.question: What does “delivery” mean in the three-layer framework?
options: Transport of residents to a park
Completion of promised physical work
Publication of household interviews
Long-term reduction of heat stress
questions.explanation: 冒号后解释为建了什么、成本多少，因此指项目实体交付完成。
questions.evidence_text: The first records delivery: what was built and at what cost.

questions.question: Why might one installed elevator produce limited benefit?
options: Old buildings never need elevators
Project counts prevent any repair work
Access, controls or maintenance may still exclude residents
Residents prefer underground pipelines
questions.explanation: 文中列出入口台阶、按钮可达性和维护成本，说明设备存在并不保证人人能持续使用。
questions.evidence_text: The project count rises by one, yet residents benefit only if the entrance is step-free, the controls are reachable and maintenance is affordable.

questions.question: What can be inferred about residents' experiences in public reporting?
options: They should be used only when no numbers exist
They make project costs impossible to compare
They are relevant only to visible projects
They help explain why identical outputs can have unequal effects
questions.explanation: 作者要求把数量与居民经验结合并解释群体差异，可推断经验资料用于揭示同一产出的不同效果。
questions.evidence_text: Good reporting should combine counts with residents' experiences and explain why benefits differ across streets or groups.

title: A Certificate Should Begin, Not End, a Career
source_title: China unveils guidelines to strengthen civil affairs services workforce
source_verification: 页面可访问；核验了养老、残疾康复、儿童福利等专业课程，校企合作与学徒制，职业标准及技能认证通道，以及2030年养老护理员持证目标等事实。
adaptation_note: 题材参考所列中国政府网英文版公开事实；本站原创改写，非媒体原文，非历年真题。
content:
Eldercare, disability rehabilitation and child welfare are sometimes described as compassionate work that depends mainly on patience. Patience matters, but the description is incomplete. A caregiver may need to recognize a change in mobility, use lifting equipment safely, communicate with a person who has cognitive impairment and record information for other professionals. These are learned skills with consequences.

A stronger certification system can make those skills visible. Clear standards tell trainees what competent practice includes, help employers compare applicants and give workers evidence when seeking promotion. School-enterprise partnerships and apprenticeships can connect classroom knowledge with real cases. Certification may also improve public respect for occupations that have often been treated as low-skilled.

Yet a certificate can become a weak symbol if the surrounding job does not support good practice. A newly qualified worker facing impossible workloads may rush a procedure learned correctly in training. An exam passed once cannot cover new equipment or changing needs for an entire career. Employers must provide supervision, continuing education and time to report mistakes without fear. Pay and progression should reward deeper competence; otherwise, experienced staff may leave.

Standards also need feedback from service users. A technically correct routine can still ignore dignity or personal preference. Complaints and observed outcomes should inform future training rather than being classified only as individual failures.

Professionalization is therefore a system, not a document. Certification establishes a common starting point. Its promise is fulfilled only when workplaces allow people to apply, question and extend what they learned.

questions.question: What is the author's main claim about professional certification in care work?
options: It is useful only when workplaces sustain and develop certified skills
It should replace supervision and continuing education
It matters less than natural patience in every situation
It can guarantee service quality through a single examination
questions.explanation: 文章肯定证书建立共同起点，但强调工作负荷、督导、继续教育、薪酬和用户反馈共同决定质量。
questions.evidence_text: Professionalization is therefore a system, not a document.

questions.question: How can apprenticeships contribute to training?
options: By allowing workers to avoid certification
By connecting classroom learning with actual cases
By replacing technical standards with personal preference
By guaranteeing immediate promotion
questions.explanation: 第二段直接说明校企合作和学徒制能连接课堂知识与真实案例。
questions.evidence_text: School-enterprise partnerships and apprenticeships can connect classroom knowledge with real cases.

questions.question: In a care career, what does progression reward after certification?
options: A sequence of care procedures
A decline in service demand
Advancement along a career path
The publication of exam results
questions.explanation: 该词与薪酬、资深员工流失并列，指职业晋升和发展通道。
questions.evidence_text: Pay and progression should reward deeper competence; otherwise, experienced staff may leave.

questions.question: Why can a technically correct routine still be inadequate?
options: Technical skills are never relevant to care
Users should design every certification exam
Correct routines always require new equipment
It may fail to respect the service user's dignity or preference
questions.explanation: 作者指出技术正确仍可能忽视尊严或个人偏好，可推断专业质量同时包含人本判断。
questions.evidence_text: A technically correct routine can still ignore dignity or personal preference.

questions.question: What does the example of impossible workloads suggest?
options: Organizational conditions can prevent trained workers from following good practice
Qualified workers no longer need time to record information
Training causes staff to rush procedures
Exams should test speed above all else
questions.explanation: 即使培训正确，过重负荷也会迫使员工匆忙操作，说明制度环境能削弱技能落实。
questions.evidence_text: A newly qualified worker facing impossible workloads may rush a procedure learned correctly in training.

title: Care Between Breakfast and Evening Pickup
source_title: Elderly daycare emerges to meet needs of Chinese families
source_verification: 页面可访问；核验了社区日间照料的餐食、活动和康复日程，认知症专项照护与用药管理，以及全日机构与居家照护之间的混合定位等事实。
adaptation_note: 题材参考所列新华社英文网公开事实；本站原创改写，非媒体原文，非历年真题。
content:
Between living independently at home and moving into a nursing institution lies a less visible form of support: elderly daycare. A resident arrives in the morning, shares meals and activities, receives therapy or hygiene assistance, and returns home when family members finish work. This timetable makes the center part of a household's daily organization rather than a permanent new address.

Its social function extends beyond supervision. Regular meals can reveal a change in appetite. Group crafts or conversation reduce isolation. For a person with cognitive impairment, a repeated schedule and medication management may lower confusion. Family caregivers gain predictable hours for employment, rest or other responsibilities. The benefits are linked: supporting the older person can also stabilize the people providing unpaid care.

Daycare nevertheless creates a boundary problem. Staff must know when a participant's needs have become too complex for the center's hours or equipment. Families need honest information rather than reassurance that delays a clinical assessment. Transport can determine access, especially for residents with limited mobility, so a nearby building is not automatically a reachable service.

Quality cannot be judged simply by attendance. A crowded activity room may look lively while offering little personal attention. Evaluation should examine safety incidents, changes in function, participant choice and caregiver strain. It should also ask whether people with lower incomes can use the service consistently.

The center's importance comes from filling a gap without pretending the gap is simple. Good daytime care connects home, family and professional support, while recognizing when another arrangement would better protect the person involved.

questions.question: How does the passage characterize elderly daycare?
options: As a complete replacement for nursing institutions
As an intermediate service linking home, family and professional care
As a social club whose success is measured by attendance
As temporary transport for employed caregivers
questions.explanation: 文章将日间照料定位为居家与机构之间的连接，并分析其对老人、家庭和专业服务的协同作用。
questions.evidence_text: Good daytime care connects home, family and professional support, while recognizing when another arrangement would better protect the person involved.

questions.question: What may regular meals help staff notice?
options: The cost of family transport
Whether a room appears crowded
A change in a participant's appetite
A caregiver's employment contract
questions.explanation: 第二段明确说规律共同用餐能暴露食欲变化。
questions.evidence_text: Regular meals can reveal a change in appetite.

questions.question: What does “stabilize” mean in paragraph two?
options: Move a person into permanent care
Increase the number of activities
Prevent all changes in health
Make daily life more manageable and steady
questions.explanation: 日间服务为家庭照护者提供可预期的工作和休息时间，因而使其生活安排更稳定可控。
questions.evidence_text: supporting the older person can also stabilize the people providing unpaid care.

questions.question: Why must staff recognize needs beyond the center's capacity?
options: False reassurance could delay more suitable assessment or care
Daycare workers should make every clinical diagnosis
Families prefer participants to remain at home alone
Complex needs always disappear after evening pickup
questions.explanation: 文中警告不能用安慰拖延临床评估，可推断边界识别关系到及时转介更合适照护。
questions.evidence_text: Families need honest information rather than reassurance that delays a clinical assessment.

questions.question: Why is a nearby center not necessarily accessible?
options: Nearby services cannot offer medication management
A person with limited mobility may still lack usable transport
Only distant centers have professional equipment
Families may mistake attendance for quality
questions.explanation: 作者指出交通决定可及性，尤其对行动受限者，物理距离近并不足够。
questions.evidence_text: Transport can determine access, especially for residents with limited mobility, so a nearby building is not automatically a reachable service.

title: A Smart Village Still Needs Local Judgment
source_title: Update: China outlines key tasks to deepen rural reforms, advance rural revitalization
source_verification: 页面可访问；核验了智慧农业和人工智能应用、冷链物流下沉乡镇、农村住房依法通过租赁或合作盘活，以及农业节水和资源管理等事实。
adaptation_note: 题材参考所列新华社英文网公开事实；本站原创改写，非媒体原文，非历年真题。
content:
Artificial intelligence, cold-chain delivery and online retail can help rural producers reach markets and manage fields. Their usefulness, however, depends on conditions that differ sharply from one place to another. A crop model trained in an irrigated plain may offer poor advice on a dry hillside. A refrigerated truck brings little value if small farms cannot gather enough produce at the right time to fill it.

This is why the phrase “according to local conditions” carries practical weight. Technology choices should begin with the problem residents identify, not with a device seeking a demonstration site. Water-saving irrigation may matter more than automation in one county. Elsewhere, a township distribution point may reduce spoilage and make e-commerce realistic. Benefits also depend on roads, electricity, repair skills and clear responsibility when a system fails.

Local judgment does not mean rejecting outside expertise. Agronomists can test new crop varieties, engineers can improve equipment and financial institutions can support investment. But farmers hold detailed knowledge about soil, weather, labor and risk. A useful project creates a way for those forms of knowledge to challenge each other before large spending begins.

Ownership deserves equal attention. Data about fields can improve forecasts, yet farmers should know who stores it and whether it may be sold. Cooperative use of rural housing or equipment can release value, but agreements must make rights, income and exit conditions understandable.

Modernization is not achieved when a village displays the newest machine. It is achieved when tools strengthen local capacity, produce durable benefits and leave residents able to shape the next decision.

title: Accessibility Tested in Motion
source_title: Feature: China empowers people with disabilities using new technology
source_verification: 页面可访问；核验了远程手语服务、无障碍模块、可调电子飞镖盘、辅助设备及赛事真实场景测试等事实。
adaptation_note: 题材参考所列新华社英文网公开事实；本站重新组织论证并原创改写，非媒体原文，非历年真题。
content:
Assistive technology is often introduced through a polished demonstration: a wheelchair crosses rough ground, a translation system recognizes a sign, or a robot guides someone around an obstacle. A sports event provides a harder test. People arrive at the same time, move between unfamiliar spaces and expect a service to work without a technician standing beside every device.

At national games for athletes with disabilities, several tools were placed inside this demanding environment. Users could request remote sign-language interpretation through video calls. Venues installed emergency buttons, accessible information platforms and translation machines linked to a central system. Electronic dartboards changed height for wheelchair users, while other exhibits included all-terrain wheelchairs and guide-dog robots.

The variety is important because “accessibility” is not one technical problem. A person may need information, physical movement, emergency assistance or communication. Improving only the entrance does little if instructions remain unavailable later. Conversely, a clever device can disappoint when it cannot connect with the venue's wider operations. Accessibility is systemic when separate parts support one another instead of leaving the user to bridge every gap.

A live event also reveals failures that a laboratory may miss. Crowds create noise; requests arrive unevenly; equipment must fit different bodies and situations. These pressures do not make public deployment an unfair test. They are precisely the conditions in which the technology is supposed to provide independence.

Yet successful operation at one event is not the final standard. Equipment requires maintenance, staff need training, and services must remain affordable after public attention moves elsewhere. Users with disabilities should participate in that evaluation, not merely appear as grateful recipients. Their reports can distinguish a feature that photographs well from one that reliably expands choice.

The strongest innovation, then, may not be a single spectacular machine. It is a network in which useful devices, responsive staff and accessible procedures continue working together when the demonstration is over.

questions.question: Which idea organizes the passage?
options: Sports events should avoid testing unfamiliar equipment
One advanced device can solve every accessibility need
Laboratory performance is the only fair measure of assistive tools
Accessibility depends on connected technology, staff and procedures in real use
questions.explanation: 全文从多类需求、系统连接、真实场景和后续维护论证无障碍必须是协同网络。
questions.evidence_text: It is a network in which useful devices, responsive staff and accessible procedures continue working together when the demonstration is over.

options: They automatically changed height
They translated speech into signs
They guided users between buildings
They sent every score to a hospital

questions.evidence_text: Electronic dartboards changed height for wheelchair users, while other exhibits included all-terrain wheelchairs and guide-dog robots.

options: Designed mainly for media photographs
Involving connected parts of a whole system
Useful only for one kind of disability

questions.explanation: 后半句解释不同部分相互支持而不是让使用者自行填补缺口，因此指系统性的。
questions.evidence_text: Accessibility is systemic when separate parts support one another instead of leaving the user to bridge every gap.

options: It guarantees that no equipment will ever fail
It allows developers to ignore maintenance costs
Its pressures resemble the real conditions in which independence is needed
Its users have exactly the same physical needs
questions.explanation: 作者指出人群、噪音和不均匀请求正是技术实际应对的条件。
questions.evidence_text: They are precisely the conditions in which the technology is supposed to provide independence.

options: Passive recipients who should simply express thanks
Temporary performers needed only for demonstrations
Customers responsible for repairing public equipment
Active evaluators whose reports should shape judgment
questions.explanation: 第五段明确反对把残障用户仅当作感恩的接受者，要求其参与评价。
questions.evidence_text: Users with disabilities should participate in that evaluation, not merely appear as grateful recipients.

title: Flexibility Without a Career Penalty
source_title: China Focus: In a changing China, parent-friendly jobs help bridge cribs and clocks
source_verification: 页面可访问；核验了中山“妈妈岗”扩展至父亲、弹性上下班与政府补贴，上海“生育友好岗”试点，以及岗位多为临时或兼职、长期发展受限等事实。
adaptation_note: 题材参考所列新华社英文网公开事实；本站原创改写，非媒体原文，非历年真题。
content:
Parent-friendly positions are usually praised for solving a scheduling conflict. A worker can leave early for kindergarten pickup, exchange hours with a colleague or complete part of a job from home. Employers may retain experienced staff, while parents avoid an unwanted exit from employment. Extending such arrangements to fathers also signals that care is not solely a mother's responsibility.

However, flexibility has two very different forms. In one, a regular position is redesigned while pay, training and promotion remain intact. In the other, the worker is moved into irregular, low-paid tasks with little chance to advance. Both may allow an afternoon pickup, but only the first challenges the assumption that serious careers require constant availability. The second merely makes the caregiver absorb the economic cost of society's schedule.

Job labels therefore need substantive standards. Employers should state pay, hours, social-insurance coverage and how performance will be assessed. Workers who use an approved flexible schedule should remain eligible for important assignments and training. Managers need methods for coordinating output rather than rewarding whoever stays visible longest. Public subsidies can encourage experimentation, but continued support should depend on retention and career outcomes, not simply the number of posts announced.

Childcare services remain essential. No work arrangement can cover a sick child, school holiday or very young infant without reliable care networks. Flexibility should complement nurseries and leave policies rather than become an excuse not to fund them.

The deeper test concerns choice over time. A parent-friendly job succeeds when a caregiver can adjust work during an intensive period and later increase hours or responsibility without carrying a permanent penalty. It should build a bridge back into a career, not a side road from which return is unusually difficult.

questions.question: What distinction about parent-friendly jobs is central to the passage?
options: Genuine flexibility preserves employment quality and future mobility
Only fathers benefit from flexible schedules
Remote work removes the need for childcare services

questions.evidence_text: In one, a regular position is redesigned while pay, training and promotion remain intact.

questions.evidence_text: Workers who use an approved flexible schedule should remain eligible for important assignments and training.

questions.question: What does “substantive” mean in the phrase “substantive standards”?

questions.explanation: 后文列出工资、工时、社保和考核等实际条件，说明该词指有真实内容而非名称。
questions.evidence_text: Job labels therefore need substantive standards.

questions.explanation: 上下文要求以产出协调而非在场时间评价，可推断可见性偏见会惩罚合理使用灵活安排者。
questions.evidence_text: Managers need methods for coordinating output rather than rewarding whoever stays visible longest.

options: Work adjustments cannot cover every care need or interruption
Nurseries determine workers' promotion eligibility
Flexible hours are intended only for school staff
Childcare services replace the need for parental leave
questions.explanation: 作者列举生病、假期和婴儿期，说明仅调工时无法承担所有照护情境。
questions.evidence_text: No work arrangement can cover a sick child, school holiday or very young infant without reliable care networks.

title: When a City Stops Growing Outward
source_title: Xi addresses Central Urban Work Conference, listing priorities for urban development
source_verification: 页面可访问；核验了城镇化从快速扩张转向存量提质，旧城更新、城市安全生命线与老化管线改造，历史文化保护，以及热线等治理机制等事实。
adaptation_note: 题材参考所列新华社英文网公开事实；本站原创改写，非媒体原文，非历年真题。
content:
Rapid urban expansion has a visible logic. New districts, roads and housing units can be counted, photographed and sold. When population growth slows and much of the necessary city already exists, the task changes. Planning must concentrate less on adding territory and more on making inherited systems safer, fairer and more useful. This transition from expansion to stewardship is technically demanding and politically less dramatic.

Existing cities contain interdependent networks. Replacing a water pipe may require digging beneath a commercial street; protecting shops can delay construction, while postponing the pipe increases failure risk. Renovating an unsafe house can displace tenants if temporary accommodation and rent rules are ignored. Preserving a historic block may support cultural identity but also attract investment that raises prices. Each improvement changes conditions around another goal.

Coordination is therefore not a ceremonial meeting among departments. Transport, housing, environmental and social-service teams need shared maps, schedules and definitions of risk. Citizen hotlines can reveal repeated failures that technical data misses, but complaint counts require interpretation: a silent neighborhood may be satisfied, excluded from the channel or tired of receiving no response.

A stewardship model also changes the time horizon. New construction is often judged at completion. Existing infrastructure must be inspected, repaired and financed repeatedly. Budgets should distinguish between cutting a ribbon and sustaining performance for decades. Public evaluation needs indicators for reliability, affordability, safety and cultural continuity, even though these are harder to summarize than square meters built.

A mature city is not one in which physical change ends. It is one that learns to intervene selectively, disclose trade-offs and correct damage before it becomes crisis. Growth then means improved capacity to care for a complex place, not simply a larger mark on the map.

questions.question: What transition in urban governance does the passage analyze?
options: From public infrastructure to privately owned services
From outward expansion to long-term stewardship of existing systems
From historic preservation to unrestricted construction
From technical planning to decisions based only on hotlines
questions.explanation: 文章围绕城市从增量扩张进入存量维护后的协调、长期资金和权衡展开。
questions.evidence_text: This transition from expansion to stewardship is technically demanding and politically less dramatic.

questions.evidence_text: Renovating an unsafe house can displace tenants if temporary accommodation and rent rules are ignored.

options: Fast construction beyond the city boundary
A ceremony marking infrastructure completion
The sale of new housing units
Responsible long-term care of existing urban assets
questions.explanation: 全文将其与持续检查、维修、资金和既有系统照管相连，指长期负责的管理。
questions.evidence_text: Planning must concentrate less on adding territory and more on making inherited systems safer, fairer and more useful.

options: Residents may lack access or confidence rather than lack problems

Satisfied neighborhoods are required to remain silent
questions.explanation: 作者列出渠道排斥和回应疲劳两种可能，说明沉默不能直接解释为满意。
questions.evidence_text: a silent neighborhood may be satisfied, excluded from the channel or tired of receiving no response.

options: Opening ceremonies are the best reliability indicator

Long-term work costs less than new construction
questions.explanation: 作者把剪彩与数十年持续绩效对照，可推断预算需包含全周期维护。
questions.evidence_text: Budgets should distinguish between cutting a ribbon and sustaining performance for decades.

title: The Riders Who Read the Street
source_title: Gig workers step up in China's grassroots governance endeavors
source_verification: 页面可访问；核验了骑手上报井盖和路灯等安全隐患、快递员与独居老人“笑脸”门牌约定，以及社区回应骑手平价餐食和换电需求等事实。
adaptation_note: 题材参考所列新华社英文网公开事实；本站原创改写，非媒体原文，非历年真题。
content:
Delivery riders and couriers possess a form of urban knowledge that rarely appears in official maps. They enter apartment compounds, notice broken lights, pass the same elderly residents and learn where a missing manhole cover creates danger after rain. A community reporting group can turn this repeated movement into early warning. The workers do not become inspectors; they add observations from places and hours formal staff may miss.

That contribution raises a question of reciprocity. Gig workers often lack affordable rest spaces, meals, battery exchange points or holiday childcare. Asking them to donate local knowledge while ignoring these conditions would treat participation as free data extraction. In one neighborhood model, officials responded to workers' reports and also created channels for their own needs. Restaurants offered lower-priced meals, and requested battery facilities were installed. Mutual response helped temporary or mobile workers see themselves as community members.

Informal observation still requires safeguards. A photograph of a damaged streetlight is different from information about a resident's private life. Volunteers need rules on consent, urgency and whom to contact. A symbol on an older person's door can support a pre-agreed welfare check, but it should not become general surveillance. Reports must be verified, and points or small rewards should not encourage quantity over accuracy.

The model also exposes an institutional blind spot. Workers whose apps measure every delivery are often described only as service providers or traffic problems. Their routes make them witnesses to how the city functions. Recognizing that knowledge does not erase the responsibility to improve labor protection; it strengthens the case for including workers in decisions that shape their working environment.

Grassroots governance benefits when participation is neither charity nor hidden labor. The community listens to workers because they know the street, and it supports them because they too have a claim on the city they help operate.

options: Workers replace professional inspectors without oversight
Communities collect delivery data in exchange for points
Workers share street knowledge while communities address their needs and rights
Riders report private information about every resident
questions.explanation: 文章主张利用骑手街区观察力的同时回应其餐饮、换电和劳动环境需求，并设置隐私边界。
questions.evidence_text: The community listens to workers because they know the street, and it supports them because they too have a claim on the city they help operate.

options: A public inspection office
A private resident database
A new delivery platform
Battery exchange facilities
questions.explanation: 第二段明确说明社区回应需求安装了换电设施。
questions.evidence_text: Restaurants offered lower-priced meals, and requested battery facilities were installed.

questions.question: What does “blind spot” mean in paragraph four?

A dangerous street without lighting
A place excluded from digital maps
A rule protecting private photographs
questions.explanation: 后文指出社会常只把平台工人视作服务者或交通问题，忽略其城市知识，故指制度性忽视。
questions.evidence_text: The model also exposes an institutional blind spot.

questions.question: Why could rewards for report quantity be harmful?
options: They prevent workers from noticing street hazards
They may encourage many weak reports rather than accurate useful ones
They make all volunteers professional inspectors
They automatically reveal residents' private lives
questions.explanation: 作者要求奖励不得让数量压过准确性，可推断错误激励会制造低质上报。
questions.evidence_text: Reports must be verified, and points or small rewards should not encourage quantity over accuracy.

questions.question: What is implied by calling participation “free data extraction”?
options: Every community report should receive a cash payment

Collecting worker knowledge without reciprocal support can be exploitative
Workers should stop sharing urgent safety information
questions.explanation: 该表述出现在社区只索取观察却忽视劳动者条件的假设中，批评单向利用。
questions.evidence_text: Asking them to donate local knowledge while ignoring these conditions would treat participation as free data extraction.

title: Fifteen Minutes for Whom?
source_title: China moves to upgrade "15-minute community life circles" to facilitate urban living
source_verification: 页面可访问；核验了步行15分钟范围内配置托育、养老、医疗、文体等服务，早餐、菜市场与维修等基本业态，以及以减租支持微利公益商户等事实。
adaptation_note: 题材参考所列新华社英文网公开事实；本站原创改写，非媒体原文，非历年真题。
content:
The “15-minute community” offers an appealing promise: daily essentials should lie within a short walk. Maps can draw circles around homes and count clinics, markets, childcare rooms or repair shops inside them. Yet geometric closeness is only the first condition of access. Fifteen minutes for a healthy adult may become forty for someone using a cane, pushing a stroller or waiting at crossings without enough time.

Service categories can also conceal quality. A point marked “eldercare” might offer only occasional activities rather than meals or bathing assistance. A clinic may be nearby but lack appointments outside working hours. A repair shop can disappear when rising rent makes a low-profit business impossible. The circle must therefore be evaluated through actual journeys, opening times, prices and service capacity, not merely addresses.

Maintaining a balanced mix creates a policy dilemma. Markets tend to favor businesses with higher returns, while breakfast stalls, small repair counters and community canteens may have strong public value but narrow margins. Rent reductions or shared premises can preserve them. Such support should use transparent eligibility and performance rules so that “public interest” does not become a permanent shield from basic quality expectations.

Residents should help define what is essential. A neighborhood with many young families may need childcare urgently; an aging block may prioritize meals and accessible health support. Aggregate demographic data provides a starting point, while walking audits and interviews reveal obstacles that averages hide. Plans also need revision as residents and commercial patterns change.

Proximity is valuable because time and physical effort shape who can participate in city life. But the number fifteen should remain a question, not a slogan. A useful life circle is one in which different residents can complete necessary journeys reliably, affordably and with dignity.

options: All essential services should operate inside one building
Residents should walk exactly fifteen minutes to every service
Commercial markets cannot provide any neighborhood service
Distance alone cannot capture usable, affordable and inclusive access

questions.question: What does “Aggregate” mean in the phrase “Aggregate demographic data”?

Combined across a population
Limited to commercial prices

questions.evidence_text: Aggregate demographic data provides a starting point, while walking audits and interviews reveal obstacles that averages hide.

questions.question: Why should public-interest businesses face performance rules?
options: Low-profit shops should be converted into clinics

questions.explanation: 作者警告公益标签不能永久保护其逃避基本质量要求，可推断扶持也需问责。
questions.evidence_text: Such support should use transparent eligibility and performance rules so that “public interest” does not become a permanent shield from basic quality expectations.

options: Every neighborhood should select a different number

questions.explanation: 结尾要求检验不同居民是否可靠、可负担且有尊严地完成出行，说明指标应接受现实验证。

title: When a Digital Service Counts as Public
source_title: China improves people's well-being through digital, intelligent services
source_verification: 页面可访问；核验了互联网医疗、电子社保卡规模及数字公共服务强调公平、普惠、可及性的事实。
adaptation_note: 题材参考所列新华社英文网公开事实；本站基于有限事实重建中心问题并原创改写，非媒体原文，非历年真题。
content:
Large user totals make a digital public service look successful. By the end of 2024, hundreds of millions of people in China were using internet-based medical services, while more than a billion held electronic social-security cards. Such figures demonstrate reach, but they do not by themselves reveal whether every user can complete a necessary task safely, understand the result, or obtain help when the system refuses a request.

This distinction matters because a public service differs from an ordinary consumer product. A shopper may leave an inconvenient application and choose another. Someone seeking medical advice, employment support or a social-security record may have no equivalent alternative. Efficiency for the provider can therefore become delay for a citizen if identity checks fail, instructions are unclear or a disability is not accommodated. The costs have not disappeared; they have migrated to the person least prepared to carry them.

A better evaluation begins by separating availability from effective access. Availability asks whether a portal exists. Effective access asks whether people with different devices, literacy levels, languages and physical abilities can reach the intended outcome. It also includes a recovery path: a telephone number, staffed desk or human review that can correct an error without forcing the user to begin again. In this context, recovery is institutional, not merely technical, because someone must be responsible for resolving the case.

Maintaining offline assistance does not mean rejecting digitization. Digital records can reduce repeated paperwork, connect agencies and shorten routine transactions. The point is to use those gains to widen service, rather than to treat the disappearance of a queue as evidence that the underlying need has disappeared. A quiet website may simply mean that excluded users stopped trying.

Public reporting should consequently combine scale with friction. Alongside total registrations, agencies can examine abandoned applications, requests for human help, correction time and differences among user groups. None of these measures is perfect, and greater collection must respect privacy. Together, however, they make invisible obstacles discussable.

A digital system earns the word public when its design recognizes obligation. It must work for ordinary cases, provide a route through exceptional ones and remain answerable to people whose needs do not fit the easiest workflow.

questions.question: What standard for digital public services does the passage propose?
options: They should combine wide reach with effective access, recovery and accountability
They should replace every staffed service as quickly as possible
They should be judged only by registration totals
They should collect unlimited personal data to prevent errors
questions.explanation: 全文从规模的局限出发，提出有效可及、纠错路径和公共责任三项标准。
questions.evidence_text: A digital system earns the word public when its design recognizes obligation.

questions.question: What is included in an effective recovery path?
options: A requirement to buy a newer device
Human help that can correct an error without a full restart
Automatic rejection of exceptional cases
Removal of every identity check
questions.explanation: 第三段直接列出电话、人工柜台或人工复核，并强调无需从头开始。
questions.evidence_text: It also includes a recovery path: a telephone number, staffed desk or human review that can correct an error without forcing the user to begin again.

questions.question: What does it mean when costs have “migrated” to the user?
options: The service has moved to another country
The application has become free
The burden has shifted rather than vanished
